cases.description: We built a tool that screens and ranks job applicants' CVs and shortlists the top candidates for recruiters.

obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system for the system.
Develop the system using training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data governance quality criteria.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation (containing at least the Annex IV elements) before placing the system on the market.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be transparent enough for deployers to interpret its output and use it appropriately, with information provided to them.
Design the system so natural persons (recruiters) can effectively oversee it while it is in use.
Ensure an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout the lifecycle.
Complete the conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI), with no notified body, before placing the system on the market.
Register yourself and the system in the EU database before placing it on the market or putting it into service.

judgements.note: Art 9(1): "shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems."
Art 10(1) requires development on training, validation and testing data sets meeting the quality criteria in paragraphs 2 to 5, which matches the obligation.
Art 11(1): drawn up before placing on the market or putting into service, kept up to date, and containing at a minimum the Annex IV elements.
Art 12(1): systems "shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system."

Art 13(1) covers design for sufficient transparency so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately. The text says nothing about providing information to deployers, which the obligation adds.
Art 14(1): designed so they "can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use." The recruiter reference is only an illustration.
Art 15(1): an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle.

Art 43(2) applies to Annex III points 2 to 8 and requires internal control under Annex VI with no notified body. Employment is Annex III point 4, so it applies. The 'before placing on the market' timing is not in this paragraph's text, but the obligation's substance is supported.

Art 49(1): before placing on the market or putting into service an Annex III system (other than point 2), the provider or authorised representative registers themselves and the system in the EU database.

critic.summary: Eight of nine obligations are grounded. Obligation 5 is misstated: Art 13(1) covers transparent design but says nothing about providing information to deployers. All core high-risk obligations are covered.

judgements.note: Art 9(1)-(2): a risk management system 'shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained' as a continuous process 'throughout the entire lifecycle'.
Art 10(1)-(3): data sets must meet quality criteria and be subject to data governance practices 'appropriate for the intended purpose'.
Art 11(1): documentation 'shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market or put into service' to demonstrate compliance.
Art 12(1)-(2): systems 'shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs)' to ensure traceability of functioning.
Art 13(1)-(3): transparency to let deployers 'interpret a system's output and use it appropriately', with accompanying instructions for use.

Art 14(1) and 14(4)(d) support effective oversight and the ability to 'disregard, override or reverse the output', but the text does not specifically require the ability to override or reverse 'grades'. It frames this generically as the output, so the grade-specific wording is added.
Art 15(1): systems must achieve 'an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity' and perform consistently 'throughout their lifecycle'.

Art 43 gives procedures by Annex III point; Art 43(2) says points 2 to 8 follow internal control under Annex VI. Education is Annex III point 3. Also, the text does not say 'before placing on the market' for the procedure, so the generic statement omits the applicable internal control route.

Art 49(1): 'Before placing on the market or putting into service a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III' (other than point 2), the provider shall register themselves and their system in the EU database.

critic.summary: Most obligations are grounded in the cited text, but two are not. Obligation 6 adds grade-specific override wording beyond Art 14's generic 'output'. Obligation 8 omits that Art 43(2) prescribes internal control under Annex VI for Annex III points 2 to 8, which includes education (point 3). No core high-risk obligations are missing.

judgements.note: Art 9(1)-(2): a risk management system 'shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained' as a continuous process 'throughout the entire lifecycle'.
Art 10(2)-(3): data sets are subject to 'data governance and management practices' and must be 'relevant, sufficiently representative'.
Art 11(1): documentation 'drawn up before that system is placed on the market or put into service and shall be kept up-to date' to demonstrate compliance.
Art 12(1)-(2): systems 'shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs)' to ensure 'traceability'.

Art 43(1) sets the conformity assessment procedures for Annex III point 1 systems. For point 7 systems, Art 43 only applies to points 2 to 8 via paragraph 2: providers follow internal control (Annex VI). The text covers conformity assessment procedures but does not state the timing 'before placing on the market or putting into service' for this obligation. Art 43(4) concerns new assessment after substantial modification. Thus the timing is not stated in the provided text.

Art 49(1): before placing on the market or putting into service an Annex III high-risk system (except point 2), the provider 'shall register themselves and their system in the EU database'. Art 49(4) places asylum/migration registration in a secure non-public section.

critic.summary: Obligations 1-7 and 9 are grounded in their cited text. Obligation 8 is not fully supported because the Art 43 text given does not state the before-market timing and, for an Annex III point 7 system, the specific procedure is the internal control route under paragraph 2.

judgements.note: Art 9(1): a risk management system "shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained" for high-risk AI systems.

Art 11(1): technical documentation "shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market or put into service and shall be kept up-to date".
Art 12(1): systems "shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system".

Art 13(1) requires operation to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret output and use it appropriately. It says nothing in this paragraph about providing information to deployers, so that duty was added.

Art 14(1): systems must be designed so they "can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use". The interview decision is the product's application of this duty.
Art 15(1): systems must achieve "an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity" and perform consistently "throughout their lifecycle".

Art 43(2) applies to systems in points 2 to 8 of Annex III, and the screening system falls under point 4. The obligation also adds a timing condition ("before placing on the market") that the provided text does not state.

Art 49(1): before placing on the market or putting into service an Annex III system (point 4 is not excepted), the provider or authorised representative "shall register themselves and their system in the EU database".

judgements.note: Art 9(1)-(2): a risk management system 'shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained' as a continuous process 'throughout the entire lifecycle'.
Art 10(3) requires data sets to be 'relevant, sufficiently representative'; Art 10(2)(f) requires 'examination in view of possible biases'.
Art 11(1): technical documentation 'shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market' and must 'demonstrate that the high-risk AI system complies'.
Art 12(1)-(2): systems 'shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs)' to ensure 'a level of traceability'.
Art 13(2) requires 'instructions for use'; Art 13(1) and 13(3)(b)(vii) cover enabling deployers to interpret output and use it appropriately.
Art 14(1) requires effective oversight 'by natural persons'; Art 14(4)(d)-(e) cover the ability to override and a 'stop' button.
Art 15(1): systems achieve 'an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity' and 'perform consistently... throughout their lifecycle'.

Art 43 text gives the procedure by Annex III point (Annex VI internal control or Annex VII with a notified body for point 1). It does not say 'before placing on the market' for conformity assessment generally, and the obligation omits the applicable-procedure conditions. For Annex III point 4, Art 43(2) mandates the Annex VI internal control procedure. The 'before placing on the market' timing is not stated in this text.
Art 49(1): 'Before placing on the market or putting into service a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III' the provider 'shall register themselves and their system in the EU database'.

Art 50(1): providers must ensure people 'are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious' to a reasonably well-informed person. The duty falls on the provider by design, but the obligation's substance matches.

critic.summary: Nine of ten obligations are supported by their cited text; obligation 8 (conformity assessment) is misstated because the cited Art 43 text does not state the timing as written and omits the procedure conditions for Annex III point 4. All core high-risk obligations are covered.
